## Architectural stack after D01

| Stack | Order | What each boundary proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity/authority | T06 canonical references → T06-HISTORY historic ownership; T07 native/Maturin authority follows T06 | One resolver across authored/generated consumers; no transferred or regressed release history; native metadata agrees with planned versions |
| Effects/retry | T08 shared physical effects → T08-RETRY tagged-candidate completion | One owner per irreversible effect; required publications gate announcements; local retry does not lose push/forge work |
| Python completion | T09 required file-set recovery → T09-ROUTES read/upload destinations | Complete declared files, not first-file presence; no changed bytes or untrusted destination on retry |
| Workflow integration | T10 intent-selected outputs → T10-NAPI lifecycle ownership | No unrelated builds or duplicate publication authority; native preparation/packing still works |
| Evidence | T12 production matrix → T12-DX measured onboarding | Executed/skipped/simulated evidence distinguished; first-release setup and credentials included in timing |

T06-HISTORY → T07 is a true stack: historical and native-authority changes share model/graph consumers. T08 follows both; T08-RETRY → T09 is also serialized because both change local/CLI release entry boundaries. Independent read-only review and native fixture drafting can run alongside those implementation units once their interfaces are fixed; competing edits cannot. T09-ROUTES follows T09 because both own the registry adapter. JSON task dependencies are authoritative; stack grouping is not permission to ignore a dependency.

## D01: decisions needed before model implementation

The owner has approved scope and direction, not every wire shape or compatibility rule. Recommendations below are proposals, not hidden release gates.

| Contract | Proposed bounded choice | Approval/evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical references | Always emit slash-qualified native IDs; retain qualified colon input as a compatibility spelling; read old bare records only through unique owned migration | Decide whether new interactive/bare CLI input is rejected or accepted with an explicit migration warning; fixtures for config, groups, changesets, pre-state and reports |
| Owner identity | Reuse a stable source-directory locator plus its explicit canonical distribution roster; do not introduce an opaque globally persistent ID | Choose a durable owner field versus deterministic derivation from the retained source snapshot; specify rename/move refusal or explicit mapping |
| Tag migration | Do not rename existing tags; retain observed legacy templates/history and select one deterministic template for new releases | Settle independent/fixed defaults with owner identity; do not add a second inference-based tag authority |
| Wire compatibility | Preserve existing string versions where context suffices; version documents whose owner/effect/output semantics change | Enumerate decision/intent/manifest/envelope/receipt readers, accepted old versions, stale decisions and old-intent rerun support; reject unsupported migration explicitly |
| Maturin | First support Cargo-owned `dynamic = ["version"]` and inherited Cargo authority with native Python mapping | Specify static co-located metadata behavior, precedence, unsupported mappings/backends and built wheel/sdist checks; do not force equal numeric strings into one grammar |
| Announcement | Current Cargo/npm/PyPI required publications before shared tag and public GitHub release; retain draft-after-tag unless a supported fixture requires otherwise | Confirm exact owner completion boundary and duplicate-effect diagnostics; future Go tag is publication, not a completion-only marker |
| Registry file set | Declare selected outputs before build; bind exact trusted filenames/digests after build without mutating sealed intent | Choose per-file effects or an aggregate operation with explicit partial-state proof; define how build inventory is covered by the existing envelope and how local retries retain original bytes |
| Python destinations | Separate credential-free index/read and upload routing; public PyPI/TestPyPI first | Choose support versus explicit refusal for custom, authenticated and HTML-only indexes; Twine credentials do not authenticate observation automatically |
| NAPI hooks | Callisto owns publication/tag/forge effects; native tooling owns build/pack preparation | Specify supported hook configuration/migration without blanket suppression of legitimate user hooks; prove a hook cannot independently publish siblings or announce |

D01 records testable contracts in the proposed architecture/ADR and PR packets. Area specs remain current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch with the behavior, and review/hash-bind that contract before a gated implementation handoff. ADR 12 stays proposed until owner acceptance and the implementing merge. No single approved future delta spec currently exists, so the portfolio JSON intentionally has no `linked_spec` or fabricated `spec_hash`; affected criterion mappings are not coverage of all 220 existing criteria.

## Stack mechanics without new infrastructure

Use ordinary Git branches/worktrees and the existing PR workflow. No stack tool was found in the inspected repository configuration; do not require a new tool to execute this plan.

- Create only authorized branches/worktrees from a committed, recorded baseline. Each worker gets a named parent revision, task packet and exclusive write set. Do not branch agents from the dirty shared checkout.
- Current CI triggers only for PRs targeting `main` in `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml`. Default: open cumulative child branches against `main`, label the dependency in the description, and include the parent-only review range. Retargeting to a parent branch would skip this CI; do not do that without a separately approved CI-trigger change.
- Review the child delta with `rtk proxy git diff <parent>...<child>`. Also inspect the complete `main`-to-child diff and run tests on the combined stack. A passing parent is not verification of its child.
- Merge parent first. Save its reviewed tip before merge; after a squash/rebase merge, replay only child commits onto updated main, using the recorded parent tip as the exclusion boundary (for example `rtk proxy git rebase --onto origin/main <recorded-parent-tip> <child-branch>`). Inspect the resulting parent-only/full diff and rerun applicable checks before merging the child. Do not assume GitHub removes ancestor commits automatically. A required force push needs explicit approval and uses `--force-with-lease`.
- Keep stacks shallow: normally two or three open dependent PRs. Merge a verified compilation boundary before extending the next model layer; do not accumulate the full architecture as one speculative stack.
- Independent lanes are sibling PRs, not artificial ancestry. Shared-interface changes land in their common parent before parallel descendants implement adapters/fixtures against those fixed interfaces.
- Each PR includes its own regression and current spec/doc amendment. Use one changeset per independent consumer-facing topic; do not add a changeset just for internal planning or duplicate a parent's changeset in a child delta.
- Commit/PR actions remain coordinator-owned and owner-approved. Workers never push, merge, approve CI, edit release policy or publish versions.

## Plugin execution route

Use a light route for existing defects and the fuller route only when a domain contract changes. Do not make every small shell patch run the complete requirement lifecycle.

| Situation | Plugins/skills | Artifact or check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Already verified current-contract defect | Navigator packet → Smith bounded implementation → Ranger targeted sibling/defect-family review → Sentinel scoped verification | Exact diff, regression/fault evidence, current criterion mapping and remaining checks |
| Canonical ownership, native authority or output-proof change | Scribe architecture/spec work and applicable audit/verify/gate steps → Navigator amendment → Smith → independent review/Sentinel | Owner-confirmed contract, versioned wire policy, interface inventory and raw spec hash |
| New domain gap discovered during implementation | Stop only that batch; Scribe architect/spec correction and Navigator amendment | Evidence-backed escalation; do not silently invent a second semantic model |
| New request beyond this scope | Weaver capture/connect/clarify only as needed | Traceable need; no unapproved requirement becomes a gate |
| User-visible release impact | Courier changeset | Verified topic-specific entry targeting `callisto-cli` |
| Commit and stacked PR handoff | Courier commit/PR after permission | Parent-only diff, full-stack evidence, base branch, migration risks and authorized remote action |

Plugins guide reasoning and evidence; they do not themselves provide isolated worktrees, a branch scheduler or authorization. Final synthesis, interface decisions and binding readiness stay with the coordinator. Sentinel must report pending/unverifiable evidence rather than converting a targeted test into a whole-release pass.

## Agent and model allocation

Prefer the host's inherited model unless a bounded job benefits from a deliberate smaller override. The currently exposed delegation runtime permits `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol` and the parent frontier model; do not rely on unavailable role-card model names or promise costs/latencies.

| Work | Allocation | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paths, symbols, test commands and branch/CI inventory | `gpt-6-luna`, low effort, recon | Read-only deterministic inventory; no architectural verdict |
| Shell installer fixtures, link/schema checks, fixed doc edits | Small model at low/medium effort where the interface is fixed | Explicit files and expected cases; escalate failed reasoning instead of lowering verification |
| Straightforward parser/lock/auth correction | Workhorse model, medium effort; raise effort for alias/auth subtleties | One subsystem, fixed owner contract and native regression |
| Canonical identity, historical authority, DAG/proofs and partial-upload semantics | Coordinator/strong model, high effort | Own cross-crate interfaces and failure semantics; no concurrent competing models |
| Implementation once interfaces are fixed | Workhorse implementer, medium/high effort | One isolated task/worktree with no shared write set |
| Independent challenge/review | Separate workhorse reviewer, high effort for model/retry changes | Read final diff plus tests; never rely on the author's self-certification |

Start with two implementing workers plus one read-only reviewer/recon, not an agent per finding. Increase concurrency only when there are disjoint, unblocked tasks and the coordinator can inspect every result. A packet contains objective, persisted paths/hashes, owned files, exclusions, criterion/test cases, dependencies and a completion condition. Workers preserve other changes and return changed paths, commands, actual outcomes, skips and unresolved concerns.

For parallel lanes, shared specs, architecture/README/operator docs, changeset creation and the repository Cargo.lock are coordinator-owned integration surfaces. Workers return proposed amendments for those files rather than editing them concurrently; the coordinator applies them on each PR branch before its final checks. Reserve shared Rust source and integration-test files explicitly before delegation; serialize packets whose write sets overlap. A forked agent conversation is not filesystem isolation: verify its actual worktree before allowing writes.

No concurrent Cargo builds/tests locally, even across tasks. Reserve one build slot; use sequential scoped runs and reuse the shared cache. Read-only analysis, shell-only tests, review and drafting can run while that slot is occupied. Worktree/build-directory changes need approval where they change environment or resource use; they are not a reason to bypass the repository's build rule.

## Interface sibling inventory

| Shared contract | Confirmed participants | Required disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Manifest` / `ManifestIdentity` / `VersionSource` | `CargoToml`, `PackageJson`, `PyprojectToml`; `read_identity`; live base-version and historical blob readers | T03-HISTORY and T07 migrate all reached readers/editors, including writers and snapshots; preserve native parsing and format rules |
| Native edges/specs | `DependencyEntry`, `DepEdge`; Cargo/npm/Python extraction; `ManifestWalkResolver::build` in `walk.rs`; cascade/floor/snapshot; fixture `InMemoryGraph` and graph test doubles | T04/T04-PNPM migrate producers, alias-aware resolution, constructors and rewrites together; correcting cascade alone cannot recover an omitted alias edge |
| Selector ownership | `IdentityIndex`; add/status/aggregate/matrix; config rules/groups; `lib.rs::sole_owner_at` and pre-state/history readers | T06/T06-HISTORY unify exact selectors, distinguish glob syntax and migrate both tag/pre-state ownership consumers |
| `ReleaseProviderSet` | Production `ValidatedReleaseIntent` and simulator `SimWorld` | T08/T09 migrate both; fake CLI provider harness still exercises real dispatch |
| Registry adapter/evidence | `CargoRegistry`, `NpmRegistry`, `PypiRegistry`; platform npm path | T09/T09-ROUTES give every reached sibling a migrated or evidence-backed unaffected disposition |
| Immutable release wires | Decision, input snapshot, intent, artifact manifest, envelope, receipt, schemas; CLI file/stdout producers and action scripts | T02 inventory; D01 fixes compatibility; T08/T09 migrate producers/consumers, including CLI registry-only inventory acceptance/envelope sealing and local build preparation |
| Selected builds and auth | Generated simple/matrix workflows, shared action execution, build matrix/placement, policy/contract tests | T10-AUTH/T10/T10-NAPI verify all routes, not just this repo's custom workflow |

This is an inspected candidate inventory, not a promise that no new call site exists. Each implementer re-runs syntactic and responsibility-based searches on its actual base. An external lifecycle hook or unavailable native environment remains an explicit coverage gap.

## Verification at each boundary

1. Record baseline and test prerequisites; write a failing reachable regression before the correction where feasible. Check the exact parent delta and structurally identical siblings.
2. Run the scoped commands in the task JSON sequentially; use native pack/install/build evidence where semantics require it. Test negative, stale, partial and conflicting states, not only a successful fresh release.
3. Review the changed diff and evidence independently. For model/proof/retry work, use a deliberate fault or mutation targeted to the changed invariant; ordinary docs/shell checks do not need a generic mutation campaign.
4. At each merge handoff, run `rtk proxy just ci` unless an explicit evidence-backed docs-only scope justifies narrower local checks; remote required checks still apply. `just ci` includes workflow contract/policy and behavior tests plus 90% coverage, but excludes actionlint, the real-binary release-PR contract and artifact-preflight builds. Run relevant excluded checks explicitly and require their CI results. Do not describe a second policy-script run as extra coverage already provided by `just ci`.
5. After restacking, repeat applicable checks on the new combined revision. Live `just provider-contract` / fixture refresh need network and are outside ordinary CI; recorded/skipped/live evidence must remain distinct.

| Fixture family | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Producer/consumer | Real decide JSON fed unchanged into verify; strict malformed/stale inputs still rejected |
| Native versions/history | Stable Python decisions and pre-state; root/inherited Cargo authority; old schemas and tamper negatives |
| Native dependencies | Promoted dual outputs; Cargo aliases/inheritance; pnpm ranges/aliases/paths/pack transforms; Python markers/extras preserved |
| Version interruption | Tracked/untracked input; late refresh/staging/decision failures; no double bump, false success or unrelated edits |
| Maturin | Co-located dynamic/static boundary; native mapping; built wheel/sdist metadata and clean installation |
| Release recovery | Tag/push/draft/upload/publication failures; full owner barrier; original trusted bytes retained |
| Registry completion | Partial Python file upload, conflicting bytes, yanked files, index lag and changed read/upload routes through production providers |
| Generated workflow | Intent-selected builds/placement, fresh native auth, unsupported builder rejection and one NAPI effect owner |
| Installation/DX | Explicit action version fidelity; complete Cargo binary inventory; fresh documented first-release timing including credentials/commits |

## Retained roadmap work: explicit disposition

- Included sibling checks: dry-run permit entry boundaries (T05/T08), alternate group-constructor conflict enforcement (T06), redacted indeterminate provider diagnostics (T08), and receipt attempt-scope wording (T12). If a reachable fix is outside its task's file boundary, record a follow-up rather than silently omit it.
- Owner decisions, not invented merge gates: workspace-wide discarded-source-error enforcement, extra npm JSON-layout preservation, stronger release-commit producer provenance, mandatory explicit registry kind and napi output attestation, private Python/HTML support, npm channels, universal registry checksums and wrapper bump severity.
- Owner/external operations: token rotation, bot-PR check policy, Rust-cache pin in `orin-dx/actions`, final migration-notice publications for retired crates and the actual v0.9/self-release. Do not perform these as side effects of implementation agents.
- Separate small follow-up, pending compatibility check: pin the floating Moon version in `.prototools`. Evaluate target facts versus the 18-triple table without adding a Rust-specific core model requirement.
- After v1 remains additive: effective-config explain, checksum sidecars/proto verification, fixed-group globs, standard archive docs and concrete Go/NuGet adapters.

docs/specs/versioning.json:71:      "criterion": "An entry name resolves to a workspace package by prefixed id (`cargo/foo`) or bare name; a bare name that matches packages in two or more ecosystems aborts the run with an ambiguous-name error (E103).",
docs/specs/versioning.json:76:      "criterion": "An entry naming a package not in the workspace, or an invalid name, produces an unknown-package warning, and a changeset with any such unresolved entry stays on disk unconsumed, even when its other entries resolve. An entry with severity `none` causes no bump and no changelog line, but its changeset is still consumed."
docs/specs/versioning.json:84:      "criterion": "`pre-major-inference` changes only inferred severity, and only for a package with a prior release tag whose current version is `0.y.z` with y >= 1: `conservative` maps major to minor, `conservative-feat` also maps minor to patch, and `off` (default) changes nothing."
docs/specs/versioning.json:97:      "criterion": "A cascaded bump has severity `bump-severity` (`patch` default, or `minor`), never lowers a severity the dependent already has, and propagates to that dependent's own dependents."
docs/specs/versioning.json:109:      "criterion": "Coverage: an exact spec covers only the equal version, a bare Cargo version is a caret requirement, a caret requirement never covers a prerelease, a Cargo `workspace = true` spec is tested using the root `[workspace.dependencies]` spec, and an npm `workspace:` shorthand (`workspace:`, `workspace:*`, `workspace:^` or `workspace:~`) always covers. A pnpm `workspace:` explicit range or exact version is tested using npm SemVer rules; an alias uses the range after its final `@`, and a relative path binds only to the admitted npm member at that directory. A catalog or other untestable spec is treated as covering and never rewritten; a catalog spec emits a CatalogSpecNotRewritten warning."
docs/specs/versioning.json:113:      "criterion": "A spec that no longer covers the new version is rewritten to it, keeping the operator and precision for Cargo and npm (`^1.2` becomes `^2.0` for 2.0.0), or to the exact version for npm when `preserve-npm-ranges = false`. A runtime, optional, build or peer dependent that is itself released in this run, for any reason, has every such spec on a bumped internal dependency raised to the dependency's new version the same way, even when the spec still covers it; a dependent that is not releasing keeps its spec unless out of range. `workspace = true`, pnpm rolling `workspace:` shorthands and catalog specs are never rewritten by either rule; an out-of-range pnpm explicit range is rewritten while retaining its `workspace:` protocol and alias. A dev dependent's spec is rewritten only when out of range. A spec that cannot be rewritten mechanically, such as an npm range with spaces, `||`, a hyphen or a wildcard, is left unchanged with a RangeNotRoundTrippable warning."
docs/specs/versioning.json:117:      "criterion": "A rewrite uses the source declaration's manifest ecosystem and preserves its declared dependency key or spelling, independent of either package's display prefix. A Cargo dependency's `package` name resolves its native target while edits retain its alias; inherited aliases resolve the workspace root's declaration. Python distribution names match using PEP 503 normalization while edits retain the spelling in the dependency declaration. A Cargo dependency inherited with `workspace = true` is rewritten in the workspace root's `[workspace.dependencies]`, not in the member manifest."
docs/specs/versioning.json:126:      "criterion": "All package members of a `[[fixed-group]]` receive the group's highest severity and one shared version, computed the same grammar- and pre-release-aware way as any other bump (VER-PRE-03): the alignment base is the on-disk version of the group's released member (a member with a release tag) if the group has one, otherwise the highest on-disk version among its members, bumped by that severity."
docs/specs/versioning.json:140:      "criterion": "When any member of a `[[linked-group]]` is bumped, every member receives the group's highest severity and all members move to the highest version any member's own bump produces (members at 1.4.0 and 2.7.3 with a minor bump both become 2.8.0)."
docs/specs/versioning.json:152:      "id": "VER-PRE-01",
docs/specs/versioning.json:153:      "criterion": "`callisto pre enter <tag>` writes `.changeset/pre.json` with `mode` `pre`, the tag, every package's current version under `initialVersions`, keyed by its display id (`foo`, or `cargo/foo` when another ecosystem has a `foo`) and an empty `changesets` list, then stages the file with git; under `--dry-run` it prints the content and writes nothing. For promoted packages, an older bare key is assigned to the unique historical owner at the commit that added pre.json; if no unique owner exists, version fails with E245."
docs/specs/versioning.json:156:      "id": "VER-PRE-02",
docs/specs/versioning.json:157:      "criterion": "`pre enter` fails when the tag is empty or whitespace, or when `.changeset/pre.json` exists with mode `pre` (also under `--dry-run`); when it exists with mode `exit`, `pre enter` instead resumes the cycle under the new tag, keeping its recorded `initialVersions` and `changesets`. `callisto pre exit` sets `mode` to `exit` and fails when the file is missing or already in `exit` mode.",
docs/specs/versioning.json:161:      "id": "VER-PRE-03",
docs/specs/versioning.json:162:      "criterion": "In pre mode, a bumped package's version is its `initialVersions` entry bumped by its severity plus `-{tag}.N`, where N starts at 0 and increments while the release part is unchanged (0.1.0 with a minor changeset and tag `beta` gives 0.2.0-beta.0, then 0.2.0-beta.1); PEP 440 packages use `aN` for tags `a`/`alpha`, `bN` for `b`/`beta`, `rcN` for `rc`/`c`/`pre`/`preview` (case-insensitive), and `.devN` for any other tag."
docs/specs/versioning.json:165:      "id": "VER-PRE-04",
docs/specs/versioning.json:166:      "criterion": "In pre mode, `version` never deletes a changeset from disk. A changeset whose id is not yet in `pre.json`'s `changesets` list counts toward severity, produces a changelog entry, and has its id added to `changesets`; a changeset whose id is already there still counts toward severity and the prerelease counter (VER-PRE-03) but produces no additional changelog entry. The `allow-empty-changesets`/`--strict` handling from VER-AGG-06 triggers only when no changeset -- new or already recorded -- resolves to a package this run, not merely when nothing new was added."
docs/specs/versioning.json:169:      "id": "VER-PRE-05",
docs/specs/versioning.json:170:      "criterion": "After `pre exit`, the next `version` moves every package at a prerelease version to its stable release (0.2.0-beta.1 becomes 0.2.0), consumes and deletes the pending changesets, and deletes `pre.json`."
docs/specs/versioning.json:173:      "id": "VER-PRE-06",
docs/specs/versioning.json:174:      "criterion": "A malformed `.changeset/pre.json` (invalid JSON, a missing `mode`, `tag`, `initialVersions` or `changesets` field, a mode other than `pre` or `exit`, or an unparsable version) makes `version` fail with E114 and write nothing; an unreadable file fails with E115.",
docs/specs/versioning.json:178:      "id": "VER-PRE-07",
docs/specs/versioning.json:182:      "id": "VER-PRE-08",
docs/specs/versioning.json:183:      "criterion": "A snapshot writes manifests and refreshes each active ecosystem's existing lockfile, unconditionally (there is no `--no-refresh-lockfiles` for `snapshot`), so a subsequent locked install resolves against the snapshot version; it ignores and keeps pending changesets, writes no changelog or `pre.json`, and stages nothing in git; under `--dry-run` it writes nothing."
docs/specs/versioning.json:186:      "id": "VER-PRE-09",
docs/specs/versioning.json:190:      "id": "VER-PRE-10",
docs/specs/versioning.json:191:      "criterion": "Every `pre.json` initial version is validated using the owning package's native grammar after historical and promoted identity resolution; the original JSON string is validated, not a spelling normalized by a cross-ecosystem fallback. A malformed owned baseline fails with E114 before version, changelog, pre-state or changeset writes during `version`, `pre exit` or resuming with `pre enter`."
docs/specs/versioning.json:216:      "criterion": "For each bumped package, apply prepends a `## {version}` section under the `# {package}` heading of its changelog (default `CHANGELOG.md` in the package directory, overridable with `changelog`), creating the file if missing and keeping CRLF line endings; a changelog that already has that heading is left unchanged."
docs/specs/versioning.json:224:      "criterion": "Outside pre mode, `version` refreshes affected lockfiles and stages written manifests, changelogs, `pre.json` changes and existing lockfiles before consuming release inputs. It stages consumed changeset and `pre.json` deletions via `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before unlinking those files from disk. If refresh, generated-state staging or input-deletion staging fails, changesets and pre-state deletion inputs remain on disk for retry."
docs/specs/versioning.json:228:      "criterion": "`version --dry-run` prints the computed plan (text output starts with `[DRY-RUN]`) and writes, deletes and stages nothing."
docs/specs/versioning.json:232:      "criterion": "`version --emit-decision <path>` writes the release decision JSON to `<path>` relative to the workspace root after the plan has been applied successfully: `schemaVersion` 2, a digest, and one entry per canonical manifest of each bumped package (ecosystem-qualified name, target version, reasons) sorted by package. Reason `kind` is `changeset`, `inference`, `fixedGroup` or `linkedGroup` (with `groupId`), `cascade` (with source package and edge kind, `peer` for peer escalation) or `preReleasePolicy` (with the prerelease tag)."
docs/specs/versioning.json:236:      "criterion": "`--emit-decision` with `--dry-run` is rejected before any work, and a plan with no bumps, or whose group members have different target versions, fails to produce a decision before any file is written.",
docs/specs/versioning.json:241:      "criterion": "A diagnostic escalated to an error (for example `--strict` on the empty-changeset warning) is evaluated right after planning: `version` writes nothing -- not the manifests and changelog, not `pre.json`, not the `--emit-decision` file -- and exits with a failure status, instead of applying the plan and only then failing.",
docs/specs/versioning.json:246:      "criterion": "Outside `mode: pre`, after planning but before any write, `version` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's on-disk effective version differs from its version at `HEAD`, or when its effective version staged in the git index differs from `HEAD`, provided a changeset remains in the `HEAD` tree or configured working-tree changesets directory (including untracked files), or a canonical manifest is staged. Staged metadata-only edits with unchanged effective versions are allowed. During `mode: exit`, already-written prerelease versions may be finalized to stable versions; a changed stable version is not exempt and is refused on retry. This detects interrupted applies without consuming retained inputs or stacking a second bump. A repository with no commits yet, a manifest/changesets directory that didn't exist at `HEAD`, or an active `mode: pre` cycle (which legitimately reruns `version` without a commit in between) is not refused this way.",
docs/specs/versioning.json:251:      "criterion": "By default, applying a plan refreshes and stages lockfiles for every ecosystem represented by an actual version, dependency, platform or optional-dependency write target, including all manifests of a dual-manifest package and workspace-root Cargo writes. It refreshes each existing lockfile: `cargo update --workspace` for Cargo; for Pypi, `uv lock` if `uv.lock` exists, else `poetry lock --no-update` if `poetry.lock` exists, else `pdm lock --update-reuse` if `pdm.lock` exists; for Npm, `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` for `package-lock.json`, `pnpm install --lockfile-only` for `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn install --mode update-lockfile` for `yarn.lock`, and `bun install --lockfile-only` for `bun.lock` or `bun.lockb`, each independently when its lockfile is present. `--no-refresh-lockfiles` skips refresh; applicable existing lockfiles are still staged."
docs/specs/versioning.json:260:      "criterion": "When E121 checks a staged canonical manifest outside prerelease mode, `version` compares its effective version in the Git index as well as the working tree against `HEAD`. It refuses if either copy contains an uncommitted version change, even when the other copy matches `HEAD`; staged metadata-only changes with the same effective version remain allowed.",

docs/publishing.md:13:### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_REDACTED`
docs/publishing.md:15:Set an `NPM_REDACTED` secret. Add this only in the protected `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:
docs/publishing.md:19:  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_REDACTED
docs/publishing.md:21:    NPM_REDACTED: ${{ secrets.NPM_REDACTED }}
docs/publishing.md:26:`npm config set` writes to the user-level `.npmrc`, which npm reads for every subsequent publish call in the same job. The version-PR action never receives this token — it only creates or updates a reviewed PR.
docs/publishing.md:30:`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_REDACTED`:
docs/publishing.md:40:    NODE_AUTH_REDACTED: ${{ secrets.NPM_REDACTED }}
docs/publishing.md:43:`NODE_AUTH_REDACTED` is silently ignored by npm unless an `.npmrc` contains a `${NODE_AUTH_REDACTED}` interpolation — that line only exists if `setup-node` ran with `registry-url` set. Setting the env var without that step fails with an auth error, not a variable-not-found error.
docs/publishing.md:47:| Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_REDACTED` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_REDACTED`) |
docs/publishing.md:50:| Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
docs/publishing.md:52:| Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |
docs/publishing.md:54:### Provenance
docs/publishing.md:56:Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.
docs/publishing.md:62:Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_REDACTED` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:
docs/publishing.md:66:  CARGO_REGISTRY_REDACTED: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_REDACTED }}
docs/publishing.md:75:Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):
docs/publishing.md:79:  TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
docs/publishing.md:80:  TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_REDACTED }}
docs/publishing.md:83:Do not use `TWINE_API_REDACTED` — twine does not recognize that variable name.
docs/publishing.md:85:The generated workflow's `PYPI_REDACTED` secret must be mapped to `TWINE_PASSWORD`; the secret's name alone is not a Twine environment variable. Keep both native auth configuration and secrets in the publishing job.
docs/publishing.md:89:The generated `release`/`execute` action step receives ecosystem tokens only during release execution. The action copies any existing npm user config to a mode-0600 temporary file, adds an npmjs token entry that interpolates `NPM_REDACTED` at publish time, and points npm-compatible clients at that file; it removes the temporary file on exit without changing the user's config. `NPM_REDACTED` remains available for existing `.npmrc` environment-variable interpolation and is withheld from Python build backends. For Bun workspaces, the action also maps it to Bun's `NPM_CONFIG_REDACTED`, since Bun does not honor npm's `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` setting. It maps `PYPI_REDACTED` to `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` and `TWINE_PASSWORD`. The Python build backend runs without registry or forge credentials; Twine receives its auth environment for upload. Cargo continues to consume `CARGO_REGISTRY_REDACTED` natively. Native package-manager publish hooks (such as `prepare` or `prepublishOnly`) retain normal package-owner-defined behavior; Callisto does not suppress or rewrite them. Npm authentication added by the action targets `registry.npmjs.org`; custom registries should use their own native configuration.
docs/publishing.md:93:Static PEP 621/Poetry versions and native `python -m build`/Twine publishing exist. Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects currently fail with E007, even when Cargo owns a dynamic Python version. Registry observation checks version presence, not whether every intended wheel and sdist is uploaded; a retry after a partial upload can incorrectly skip the rest.
docs/publishing.md:95:The configured Python registry URL is currently reused for simple-index reads and Twine uploads. Private registries with separate read/upload routes, read authentication or HTML-only indexes need an explicit supported setup; Twine credentials do not configure `curl` automatically. The native argv tests against a local pypiserver do not prove the production binding/observation path supports every such server.

use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;

use callisto_model::format::{parse_pre_json, write_pre_json, write_pre_json_preserving, PreMode, PreState};
use callisto_model::{ApplyPermit, CommandRunner, PreReport, SCHEMA_VERSION};

use crate::cli::{GlobalArgs, OutputFormat, PreArgs};
use crate::error::CliError;
use crate::output::{emit_line, emit_report, log_line};
use crate::runner::CliCommandRunner;
use crate::workspace::load_workspace;

/// Extracted from [`handle`] so a fake [`CommandRunner`] can exercise the `git add` without shelling out for real.
fn stage_pre_json(runner: &dyn CommandRunner, root: &Path, rel_path: &Path) -> Result<(), CliError> {
    let rel_str = rel_path.to_string_lossy();
    let output = runner.run("git", &["add", rel_str.as_ref()], root)?;
    if !output.success() {
        return Err(callisto_model::CommandError::Failed {
            program: "git".to_string(),
            exit_code: output.exit_code,
            stderr: output.redacted_stderr(),
        }
        .into());
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Mirrors `add`'s dry-run preview so both commands report the not-yet-written content the same way.
fn preview(global: &GlobalArgs, mode: &str, tag: &str, rel_path: &Path, content: &str) -> Result<(), CliError> {
    let rel_str = rel_path.to_string_lossy();
    match global.format {
        OutputFormat::Json => {
            let report = PreReport {
                schema_version: SCHEMA_VERSION,
                mode: mode.to_string(),
                tag: tag.to_string(),
                path: Some(rel_str.into_owned()),
                content: Some(content.to_string()),
                diagnostics: vec![],
            };
            emit_report(&mut std::io::stdout(), &report, true)?;
        }
        OutputFormat::Text => {
            emit_line(&format!(
                "[DRY-RUN] Would write {rel_str} (no files written)\n\n{content}"
            ))?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Handles the `pre enter` and `pre exit` subcommands.
///
/// `pre enter` writes `.changeset/pre.json` with the supplied tag and a snapshot
/// of current package versions. `pre exit` updates an existing `pre.json`'s mode
/// to `exit`. Under `--dry-run`, neither subcommand writes any file; instead the
/// would-be content is rendered to stdout.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`CliError::PreAlreadyActive`] if `enter` runs while `pre.json`'s mode
/// is already `pre`, and [`CliError::PreNotActive`] if `exit` runs with no
/// `pre.json` on disk. Otherwise returns [`CliError::Io`] if reading an existing
/// `pre.json` fails, or if any write fails (`enter` subcommand on a real run).
pub fn handle(args: PreArgs, global: &GlobalArgs) -> Result<ExitCode, CliError> {
    let runner = CliCommandRunner;
    let permit = ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(global.dry_run);

    match args {
        PreArgs::Enter { tag } => {
            // Bug 3: reject empty tags before any workspace I/O.
            if tag.trim().is_empty() {
                return Err(CliError::PreTagEmpty);
            }

            let ws = load_workspace(global, &runner)?;

            // Reject re-entering only while a cycle is actually active (mode `pre`); a `pre.json` left
            // behind in `exit` mode is a finished cycle, so entering starts a new one from where it
            // left off instead of erroring on a file that merely still exists on disk.
            let rel_pre_path = ws.config.pre_json_path();
            let pre_path = ws.root.join(&rel_pre_path);
            let pre_dir = pre_path.parent().unwrap_or(&ws.root).to_path_buf();
            let pre_state = if pre_path.exists() {
                let existing_text = fs::read_to_string(&pre_path).map_err(|source| CliError::Io {
                    source,
                    path: Some(pre_path.clone()),
                })?;
                let existing = parse_pre_json(&existing_text)?;
                if existing.mode == PreMode::Pre {
                    return Err(CliError::PreAlreadyActive);
                }
                let existing = ws.resolve_pre_state_from_json(existing, &existing_text)?;
                // Re-entering after `exit` carries the same initial-versions baseline and recorded
                // changesets forward under the new tag, matching a resumed rather than a fresh cycle.
                PreState {
                    mode: PreMode::Pre,
                    tag: tag.clone(),
                    ..existing
                }
            } else {
                let initial = ws.initial_versions()?;
                let mut snapshot = indexmap::IndexMap::new();
                for (k, v) in initial {
                    snapshot.insert(k, v);
                }
                PreState::entering(tag.clone(), snapshot)
            };
            let text = write_pre_json(&pre_state);

            let Some(permit) = permit else {
                preview(global, "pre", &tag, &rel_pre_path, &text)?;
                return Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS);
            };

            fs::create_dir_all(&pre_dir)?;
            callisto_manifests::atomic::atomic_write(&pre_path, &text, &permit)?;

            // Bug 4: stage pre.json so it is included in the next commit.
            stage_pre_json(&runner, &ws.root, &rel_pre_path)?;

            match global.format {
                OutputFormat::Json => {
                    let report = PreReport {
                        schema_version: SCHEMA_VERSION,
                        mode: "pre".to_string(),
                        tag: tag.clone(),
                        path: None,
                        content: None,
                        diagnostics: vec![],
                    };
                    emit_report(&mut std::io::stdout(), &report, false)?;
                }
                OutputFormat::Text => {
                    log_line(global.format, &format!("Entered pre mode with tag `{tag}`"))?;
                }
            }
        }
        PreArgs::Exit => {
            let start = dunce::canonicalize(&global.cwd).map_err(|source| CliError::Io {
                source,
                path: Some(global.cwd.clone()),
            })?;
            let root = callisto_graph::locate::find_workspace_root(&start, &runner)?;
            let config = callisto_graph::load_config(&root)?;
            let rel_pre_path = config.pre_json_path();
            let pre_path = root.join(&rel_pre_path);

            if !pre_path.exists() {
                return Err(CliError::PreNotActive);
            }
            let text = fs::read_to_string(&pre_path).map_err(|source| CliError::Io {
                source,
                path: Some(pre_path.clone()),
            })?;
            let mut pre_state = parse_pre_json(&text)?;

            // Reject double-exit.
            if pre_state.mode == PreMode::Exit {
                return Err(CliError::PreAlreadyExited);
            }

            let ws = load_workspace(global, &runner)?;
            pre_state = ws.resolve_pre_state_from_json(pre_state, &text)?;
            pre_state.mode = PreMode::Exit;

            let updated = write_pre_json_preserving(&pre_state, &text);

            let Some(permit) = permit else {
                preview(global, "exit", &pre_state.tag, &rel_pre_path, &updated)?;
                return Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS);
            };

            callisto_manifests::atomic::atomic_write(&pre_path, &updated, &permit)?;

            // Mutates the same tracked file `pre enter` created, so it must be staged the same way.
            stage_pre_json(&runner, &root, &rel_pre_path)?;

            match global.format {
                OutputFormat::Json => {
                    let report = PreReport {
                        schema_version: SCHEMA_VERSION,
                        mode: "exit".to_string(),
                        tag: pre_state.tag.clone(),
                        path: None,
                        content: None,
                        diagnostics: vec![],
                    };
                    emit_report(&mut std::io::stdout(), &report, false)?;
                }
                OutputFormat::Text => {
                    log_line(global.format, "Exiting pre mode")?;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
}

mod tests {

    use callisto_model::{CommandError, CommandOutput, CommandRunner};

    use super::{handle, stage_pre_json};
    use crate::cli::{GlobalArgs, OutputFormat, PreArgs};

    /// `pre enter --dry-run --format text` must not write `.changeset/pre.json`

        let tmp = tempfile::TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let root = tmp.path();
        callisto_fixtures::git::init_repo(root);
        std::fs::write(root.join("Cargo.toml"), "[workspace]\nmembers = []\nresolver = \"2\"\n").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(root.join("callisto.toml"), "").unwrap();

        let global = GlobalArgs {
            format: OutputFormat::Text,
            cwd: root.to_path_buf(),
            dry_run: true,
        };

        let result = handle(
            PreArgs::Enter {
                tag: "beta".to_string(),
            },

        assert!(result.is_ok(), "expected Ok, got: {result:?}");

        assert!(
            !root.join(".changeset/pre.json").exists(),
            "dry-run must not write pre.json"
        );
    }

T01, T05 and T11 follow-up reviews found no remaining defects. The remaining implementation is local and no PR stack has been opened. Architectural D01 choices, remote PR delivery and publication remain separate decisions.

## PR-sized lanes and current position

| Lane | PR-sized units | Dependency or constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release/wire | T01 producer/consumer fix → T02 schema repair → T03 contextual decisions → T03-PRE baselines; T03-HISTORY inherited/root verification follows T03 and T04 | T01 fix is committed; other units local; stack separation remains |
| Native resolution | T04 manifest-local names → T04-PNPM protocols → T04-LOCK refresh | Implemented locally; review corrections closed; stack separation remains |
| Installer | T11 version/source fidelity | Committed locally as `a37025927`; independent review and combined full CI pass |
| Early workflows | T10-BINS binary inventory/unsupported builders → T10-AUTH native auth | Both implemented locally; lifecycle-script trust boundary should be explicit in handoff/docs |
| Apply recovery join | T05 input retention and partial-run detection | Implemented with staging/retry regressions; independent follow-up review found no remaining findings |

T01 is the v0.9 release-path priority. Its merge permits the bot to regenerate the release PR; fresh decision/source agreement and passing CI must precede any separately authorized merge/publication. Other lanes do not automatically become v0.9 release requirements. Existing-contract fixes can run while the architectural decisions below are being reviewed.

## Architectural stack after D01

| Stack | Order | What each boundary proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity/authority | T06 canonical references → T06-HISTORY historic ownership; T07 native/Maturin authority follows T06 | One resolver across authored/generated consumers; no transferred or regressed release history; native metadata agrees with planned versions |
| Effects/retry | T08 shared physical effects → T08-RETRY tagged-candidate completion | One owner per irreversible effect; required publications gate announcements; local retry does not lose push/forge work |
| Python completion | T09 required file-set recovery → T09-ROUTES read/upload destinations | Complete declared files, not first-file presence; no changed bytes or untrusted destination on retry |
| Workflow integration | T10 intent-selected outputs → T10-NAPI lifecycle ownership | No unrelated builds or duplicate publication authority; native preparation/packing still works |
| Evidence | T12 production matrix → T12-DX measured onboarding | Executed/skipped/simulated evidence distinguished; first-release setup and credentials included in timing |

T06-HISTORY → T07 is a true stack: historical and native-authority changes share model/graph consumers. T08 follows both; T08-RETRY → T09 is also serialized because both change local/CLI release entry boundaries. Independent read-only review and native fixture drafting can run alongside those implementation units once their interfaces are fixed; competing edits cannot. T09-ROUTES follows T09 because both own the registry adapter. JSON task dependencies are authoritative; stack grouping is not permission to ignore a dependency.

## D01: decisions needed before model implementation

The owner has approved scope and direction, not every wire shape or compatibility rule. Recommendations below are proposals, not hidden release gates.

| Contract | Proposed bounded choice | Approval/evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical references | Always emit slash-qualified native IDs; retain qualified colon input as a compatibility spelling; read old bare records only through unique owned migration | Decide whether new interactive/bare CLI input is rejected or accepted with an explicit migration warning; fixtures for config, groups, changesets, pre-state and reports |
| Owner identity | Reuse a stable source-directory locator plus its explicit canonical distribution roster; do not introduce an opaque globally persistent ID | Choose a durable owner field versus deterministic derivation from the retained source snapshot; specify rename/move refusal or explicit mapping |
| Tag migration | Do not rename existing tags; retain observed legacy templates/history and select one deterministic template for new releases | Settle independent/fixed defaults with owner identity; do not add a second inference-based tag authority |
| Wire compatibility | Preserve existing string versions where context suffices; version documents whose owner/effect/output semantics change | Enumerate decision/intent/manifest/envelope/receipt readers, accepted old versions, stale decisions and old-intent rerun support; reject unsupported migration explicitly |
| Maturin | First support Cargo-owned `dynamic = ["version"]` and inherited Cargo authority with native Python mapping | Specify static co-located metadata behavior, precedence, unsupported mappings/backends and built wheel/sdist checks; do not force equal numeric strings into one grammar |
| Announcement | Current Cargo/npm/PyPI required publications before shared tag and public GitHub release; retain draft-after-tag unless a supported fixture requires otherwise | Confirm exact owner completion boundary and duplicate-effect diagnostics; future Go tag is publication, not a completion-only marker |
| Registry file set | Declare selected outputs before build; bind exact trusted filenames/digests after build without mutating sealed intent | Choose per-file effects or an aggregate operation with explicit partial-state proof; define how build inventory is covered by the existing envelope and how local retries retain original bytes |
| Python destinations | Separate credential-free index/read and upload routing; public PyPI/TestPyPI first | Choose support versus explicit refusal for custom, authenticated and HTML-only indexes; Twine credentials do not authenticate observation automatically |
| NAPI hooks | Callisto owns publication/tag/forge effects; native tooling owns build/pack preparation | Specify supported hook configuration/migration without blanket suppression of legitimate user hooks; prove a hook cannot independently publish siblings or announce |

D01 records testable contracts in the proposed architecture/ADR and PR packets. Area specs remain current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch with the behavior, and review/hash-bind that contract before a gated implementation handoff. ADR 12 stays proposed until owner acceptance and the implementing merge. No single approved future delta spec currently exists, so the portfolio JSON intentionally has no `linked_spec` or fabricated `spec_hash`; affected criterion mappings are not coverage of all 220 existing criteria.

## Stack mechanics without new infrastructure

Use ordinary Git branches/worktrees and the existing PR workflow. No stack tool was found in the inspected repository configuration; do not require a new tool to execute this plan.

- Create only authorized branches/worktrees from a committed, recorded baseline. Each worker gets a named parent revision, task packet and exclusive write set. Do not branch agents from the dirty shared checkout.
- Current CI triggers only for PRs targeting `main` in `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml`. Default: open cumulative child branches against `main`, label the dependency in the description, and include the parent-only review range. Retargeting to a parent branch would skip this CI; do not do that without a separately approved CI-trigger change.
- Review the child delta with `rtk proxy git diff <parent>...<child>`. Also inspect the complete `main`-to-child diff and run tests on the combined stack. A passing parent is not verification of its child.
- Merge parent first. Save its reviewed tip before merge; after a squash/rebase merge, replay only child commits onto updated main, using the recorded parent tip as the exclusion boundary (for example `rtk proxy git rebase --onto origin/main <recorded-parent-tip> <child-branch>`). Inspect the resulting parent-only/full diff and rerun applicable checks before merging the child. Do not assume GitHub removes ancestor commits automatically. A required force push needs explicit approval and uses `--force-with-lease`.
- Keep stacks shallow: normally two or three open dependent PRs. Merge a verified compilation boundary before extending the next model layer; do not accumulate the full architecture as one speculative stack.
- Independent lanes are sibling PRs, not artificial ancestry. Shared-interface changes land in their common parent before parallel descendants implement adapters/fixtures against those fixed interfaces.
- Each PR includes its own regression and current spec/doc amendment. Use one changeset per independent consumer-facing topic; do not add a changeset just for internal planning or duplicate a parent's changeset in a child delta.
- Commit/PR actions remain coordinator-owned and owner-approved. Workers never push, merge, approve CI, edit release policy or publish versions.

## Plugin execution route

Use a light route for existing defects and the fuller route only when a domain contract changes. Do not make every small shell patch run the complete requirement lifecycle.

| Situation | Plugins/skills | Artifact or check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Already verified current-contract defect | Navigator packet → Smith bounded implementation → Ranger targeted sibling/defect-family review → Sentinel scoped verification | Exact diff, regression/fault evidence, current criterion mapping and remaining checks |
| Canonical ownership, native authority or output-proof change | Scribe architecture/spec work and applicable audit/verify/gate steps → Navigator amendment → Smith → independent review/Sentinel | Owner-confirmed contract, versioned wire policy, interface inventory and raw spec hash |
| New domain gap discovered during implementation | Stop only that batch; Scribe architect/spec correction and Navigator amendment | Evidence-backed escalation; do not silently invent a second semantic model |
| New request beyond this scope | Weaver capture/connect/clarify only as needed | Traceable need; no unapproved requirement becomes a gate |
| User-visible release impact | Courier changeset | Verified topic-specific entry targeting `callisto-cli` |
| Commit and stacked PR handoff | Courier commit/PR after permission | Parent-only diff, full-stack evidence, base branch, migration risks and authorized remote action |

Plugins guide reasoning and evidence; they do not themselves provide isolated worktrees, a branch scheduler or authorization. Final synthesis, interface decisions and binding readiness stay with the coordinator. Sentinel must report pending/unverifiable evidence rather than converting a targeted test into a whole-release pass.

## Agent and model allocation

Prefer the host's inherited model unless a bounded job benefits from a deliberate smaller override. The currently exposed delegation runtime permits `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol` and the parent frontier model; do not rely on unavailable role-card model names or promise costs/latencies.

| Work | Allocation | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paths, symbols, test commands and branch/CI inventory | `gpt-6-luna`, low effort, recon | Read-only deterministic inventory; no architectural verdict |
| Shell installer fixtures, link/schema checks, fixed doc edits | Small model at low/medium effort where the interface is fixed | Explicit files and expected cases; escalate failed reasoning instead of lowering verification |
| Straightforward parser/lock/auth correction | Workhorse model, medium effort; raise effort for alias/auth subtleties | One subsystem, fixed owner contract and native regression |
| Canonical identity, historical authority, DAG/proofs and partial-upload semantics | Coordinator/strong model, high effort | Own cross-crate interfaces and failure semantics; no concurrent competing models |
| Implementation once interfaces are fixed | Workhorse implementer, medium/high effort | One isolated task/worktree with no shared write set |
| Independent challenge/review | Separate workhorse reviewer, high effort for model/retry changes | Read final diff plus tests; never rely on the author's self-certification |

Start with two implementing workers plus one read-only reviewer/recon, not an agent per finding. Increase concurrency only when there are disjoint, unblocked tasks and the coordinator can inspect every result. A packet contains objective, persisted paths/hashes, owned files, exclusions, criterion/test cases, dependencies and a completion condition. Workers preserve other changes and return changed paths, commands, actual outcomes, skips and unresolved concerns.

For parallel lanes, shared specs, architecture/README/operator docs, changeset creation and the repository Cargo.lock are coordinator-owned integration surfaces. Workers return proposed amendments for those files rather than editing them concurrently; the coordinator applies them on each PR branch before its final checks. Reserve shared Rust source and integration-test files explicitly before delegation; serialize packets whose write sets overlap. A forked agent conversation is not filesystem isolation: verify its actual worktree before allowing writes.

No concurrent Cargo builds/tests locally, even across tasks. Reserve one build slot; use sequential scoped runs and reuse the shared cache. Read-only analysis, shell-only tests, review and drafting can run while that slot is occupied. Worktree/build-directory changes need approval where they change environment or resource use; they are not a reason to bypass the repository's build rule.

## Interface sibling inventory

| Shared contract | Confirmed participants | Required disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Manifest` / `ManifestIdentity` / `VersionSource` | `CargoToml`, `PackageJson`, `PyprojectToml`; `read_identity`; live base-version and historical blob readers | T03-HISTORY and T07 migrate all reached readers/editors, including writers and snapshots; preserve native parsing and format rules |
| Native edges/specs | `DependencyEntry`, `DepEdge`; Cargo/npm/Python extraction; `ManifestWalkResolver::build` in `walk.rs`; cascade/floor/snapshot; fixture `InMemoryGraph` and graph test doubles | T04/T04-PNPM migrate producers, alias-aware resolution, constructors and rewrites together; correcting cascade alone cannot recover an omitted alias edge |
| Selector ownership | `IdentityIndex`; add/status/aggregate/matrix; config rules/groups; `lib.rs::sole_owner_at` and pre-state/history readers | T06/T06-HISTORY unify exact selectors, distinguish glob syntax and migrate both tag/pre-state ownership consumers |
| `ReleaseProviderSet` | Production `ValidatedReleaseIntent` and simulator `SimWorld` | T08/T09 migrate both; fake CLI provider harness still exercises real dispatch |
| Registry adapter/evidence | `CargoRegistry`, `NpmRegistry`, `PypiRegistry`; platform npm path | T09/T09-ROUTES give every reached sibling a migrated or evidence-backed unaffected disposition |
| Immutable release wires | Decision, input snapshot, intent, artifact manifest, envelope, receipt, schemas; CLI file/stdout producers and action scripts | T02 inventory; D01 fixes compatibility; T08/T09 migrate producers/consumers, including CLI registry-only inventory acceptance/envelope sealing and local build preparation |
| Selected builds and auth | Generated simple/matrix workflows, shared action execution, build matrix/placement, policy/contract tests | T10-AUTH/T10/T10-NAPI verify all routes, not just this repo's custom workflow |

This is an inspected candidate inventory, not a promise that no new call site exists. Each implementer re-runs syntactic and responsibility-based searches on its actual base. An external lifecycle hook or unavailable native environment remains an explicit coverage gap.

## Verification at each boundary

1. Record baseline and test prerequisites; write a failing reachable regression before the correction where feasible. Check the exact parent delta and structurally identical siblings.
2. Run the scoped commands in the task JSON sequentially; use native pack/install/build evidence where semantics require it. Test negative, stale, partial and conflicting states, not only a successful fresh release.
3. Review the changed diff and evidence independently. For model/proof/retry work, use a deliberate fault or mutation targeted to the changed invariant; ordinary docs/shell checks do not need a generic mutation campaign.
4. At each merge handoff, run `rtk proxy just ci` unless an explicit evidence-backed docs-only scope justifies narrower local checks; remote required checks still apply. `just ci` includes workflow contract/policy and behavior tests plus 90% coverage, but excludes actionlint, the real-binary release-PR contract and artifact-preflight builds. Run relevant excluded checks explicitly and require their CI results. Do not describe a second policy-script run as extra coverage already provided by `just ci`.
5. After restacking, repeat applicable checks on the new combined revision. Live `just provider-contract` / fixture refresh need network and are outside ordinary CI; recorded/skipped/live evidence must remain distinct.

| Fixture family | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Producer/consumer | Real decide JSON fed unchanged into verify; strict malformed/stale inputs still rejected |
| Native versions/history | Stable Python decisions and pre-state; root/inherited Cargo authority; old schemas and tamper negatives |
| Native dependencies | Promoted dual outputs; Cargo aliases/inheritance; pnpm ranges/aliases/paths/pack transforms; Python markers/extras preserved |
| Version interruption | Tracked/untracked input; late refresh/staging/decision failures; no double bump, false success or unrelated edits |
| Maturin | Co-located dynamic/static boundary; native mapping; built wheel/sdist metadata and clean installation |
| Release recovery | Tag/push/draft/upload/publication failures; full owner barrier; original trusted bytes retained |
| Registry completion | Partial Python file upload, conflicting bytes, yanked files, index lag and changed read/upload routes through production providers |
| Generated workflow | Intent-selected builds/placement, fresh native auth, unsupported builder rejection and one NAPI effect owner |
| Installation/DX | Explicit action version fidelity; complete Cargo binary inventory; fresh documented first-release timing including credentials/commits |

## Retained roadmap work: explicit disposition

- Included sibling checks: dry-run permit entry boundaries (T05/T08), alternate group-constructor conflict enforcement (T06), redacted indeterminate provider diagnostics (T08), and receipt attempt-scope wording (T12). If a reachable fix is outside its task's file boundary, record a follow-up rather than silently omit it.
- Owner decisions, not invented merge gates: workspace-wide discarded-source-error enforcement, extra npm JSON-layout preservation, stronger release-commit producer provenance, mandatory explicit registry kind and napi output attestation, private Python/HTML support, npm channels, universal registry checksums and wrapper bump severity.
- Owner/external operations: token rotation, bot-PR check policy, Rust-cache pin in `orin-dx/actions`, final migration-notice publications for retired crates and the actual v0.9/self-release. Do not perform these as side effects of implementation agents.
- Separate small follow-up, pending compatibility check: pin the floating Moon version in `.prototools`. Evaluate target facts versus the 18-triple table without adding a Rust-specific core model requirement.
- After v1 remains additive: effective-config explain, checksum sidecars/proto verification, fixed-group globs, standard archive docs and concrete Go/NuGet adapters.

## Architectural stack after D01

| Stack | Order | What each boundary proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity/authority | T06 canonical references → T06-HISTORY historic ownership; T07 native/Maturin authority follows T06 | One resolver across authored/generated consumers; no transferred or regressed release history; native metadata agrees with planned versions |
| Effects/retry | T08 shared physical effects → T08-RETRY tagged-candidate completion | One owner per irreversible effect; required publications gate announcements; local retry does not lose push/forge work |
| Python completion | T09 required file-set recovery → T09-ROUTES read/upload destinations | Complete declared files, not first-file presence; no changed bytes or untrusted destination on retry |
| Workflow integration | T10 intent-selected outputs → T10-NAPI lifecycle ownership | No unrelated builds or duplicate publication authority; native preparation/packing still works |
| Evidence | T12 production matrix → T12-DX measured onboarding | Executed/skipped/simulated evidence distinguished; first-release setup and credentials included in timing |

T06-HISTORY → T07 is a true stack: historical and native-authority changes share model/graph consumers. T08 follows both; T08-RETRY → T09 is also serialized because both change local/CLI release entry boundaries. Independent read-only review and native fixture drafting can run alongside those implementation units once their interfaces are fixed; competing edits cannot. T09-ROUTES follows T09 because both own the registry adapter. JSON task dependencies are authoritative; stack grouping is not permission to ignore a dependency.

## D01: decisions needed before model implementation

The owner has approved scope and direction, not every wire shape or compatibility rule. Recommendations below are proposals, not hidden release gates.

| Contract | Proposed bounded choice | Approval/evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical references | Always emit slash-qualified native IDs; retain qualified colon input as a compatibility spelling; read old bare records only through unique owned migration | Decide whether new interactive/bare CLI input is rejected or accepted with an explicit migration warning; fixtures for config, groups, changesets, pre-state and reports |
| Owner identity | Reuse a stable source-directory locator plus its explicit canonical distribution roster; do not introduce an opaque globally persistent ID | Choose a durable owner field versus deterministic derivation from the retained source snapshot; specify rename/move refusal or explicit mapping |
| Tag migration | Do not rename existing tags; retain observed legacy templates/history and select one deterministic template for new releases | Settle independent/fixed defaults with owner identity; do not add a second inference-based tag authority |
| Wire compatibility | Preserve existing string versions where context suffices; version documents whose owner/effect/output semantics change | Enumerate decision/intent/manifest/envelope/receipt readers, accepted old versions, stale decisions and old-intent rerun support; reject unsupported migration explicitly |
| Maturin | First support Cargo-owned `dynamic = ["version"]` and inherited Cargo authority with native Python mapping | Specify static co-located metadata behavior, precedence, unsupported mappings/backends and built wheel/sdist checks; do not force equal numeric strings into one grammar |
| Announcement | Current Cargo/npm/PyPI required publications before shared tag and public GitHub release; retain draft-after-tag unless a supported fixture requires otherwise | Confirm exact owner completion boundary and duplicate-effect diagnostics; future Go tag is publication, not a completion-only marker |
| Registry file set | Declare selected outputs before build; bind exact trusted filenames/digests after build without mutating sealed intent | Choose per-file effects or an aggregate operation with explicit partial-state proof; define how build inventory is covered by the existing envelope and how local retries retain original bytes |
| Python destinations | Separate credential-free index/read and upload routing; public PyPI/TestPyPI first | Choose support versus explicit refusal for custom, authenticated and HTML-only indexes; Twine credentials do not authenticate observation automatically |
| NAPI hooks | Callisto owns publication/tag/forge effects; native tooling owns build/pack preparation | Specify supported hook configuration/migration without blanket suppression of legitimate user hooks; prove a hook cannot independently publish siblings or announce |

D01 records testable contracts in the proposed architecture/ADR and PR packets. Area specs remain current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch with the behavior, and review/hash-bind that contract before a gated implementation handoff. ADR 12 stays proposed until owner acceptance and the implementing merge. No single approved future delta spec currently exists, so the portfolio JSON intentionally has no `linked_spec` or fabricated `spec_hash`; affected criterion mappings are not coverage of all 220 existing criteria.

## Stack mechanics without new infrastructure

Use ordinary Git branches/worktrees and the existing PR workflow. No stack tool was found in the inspected repository configuration; do not require a new tool to execute this plan.

- Create only authorized branches/worktrees from a committed, recorded baseline. Each worker gets a named parent revision, task packet and exclusive write set. Do not branch agents from the dirty shared checkout.
- Current CI triggers only for PRs targeting `main` in `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml`. Default: open cumulative child branches against `main`, label the dependency in the description, and include the parent-only review range. Retargeting to a parent branch would skip this CI; do not do that without a separately approved CI-trigger change.
- Review the child delta with `rtk proxy git diff <parent>...<child>`. Also inspect the complete `main`-to-child diff and run tests on the combined stack. A passing parent is not verification of its child.
- Merge parent first. Save its reviewed tip before merge; after a squash/rebase merge, replay only child commits onto updated main, using the recorded parent tip as the exclusion boundary (for example `rtk proxy git rebase --onto origin/main <recorded-parent-tip> <child-branch>`). Inspect the resulting parent-only/full diff and rerun applicable checks before merging the child. Do not assume GitHub removes ancestor commits automatically. A required force push needs explicit approval and uses `--force-with-lease`.
- Keep stacks shallow: normally two or three open dependent PRs. Merge a verified compilation boundary before extending the next model layer; do not accumulate the full architecture as one speculative stack.
- Independent lanes are sibling PRs, not artificial ancestry. Shared-interface changes land in their common parent before parallel descendants implement adapters/fixtures against those fixed interfaces.
- Each PR includes its own regression and current spec/doc amendment. Use one changeset per independent consumer-facing topic; do not add a changeset just for internal planning or duplicate a parent's changeset in a child delta.
- Commit/PR actions remain coordinator-owned and owner-approved. Workers never push, merge, approve CI, edit release policy or publish versions.

## Plugin execution route

Use a light route for existing defects and the fuller route only when a domain contract changes. Do not make every small shell patch run the complete requirement lifecycle.

| Situation | Plugins/skills | Artifact or check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Already verified current-contract defect | Navigator packet → Smith bounded implementation → Ranger targeted sibling/defect-family review → Sentinel scoped verification | Exact diff, regression/fault evidence, current criterion mapping and remaining checks |
| Canonical ownership, native authority or output-proof change | Scribe architecture/spec work and applicable audit/verify/gate steps → Navigator amendment → Smith → independent review/Sentinel | Owner-confirmed contract, versioned wire policy, interface inventory and raw spec hash |
| New domain gap discovered during implementation | Stop only that batch; Scribe architect/spec correction and Navigator amendment | Evidence-backed escalation; do not silently invent a second semantic model |
| New request beyond this scope | Weaver capture/connect/clarify only as needed | Traceable need; no unapproved requirement becomes a gate |
| User-visible release impact | Courier changeset | Verified topic-specific entry targeting `callisto-cli` |
| Commit and stacked PR handoff | Courier commit/PR after permission | Parent-only diff, full-stack evidence, base branch, migration risks and authorized remote action |

Plugins guide reasoning and evidence; they do not themselves provide isolated worktrees, a branch scheduler or authorization. Final synthesis, interface decisions and binding readiness stay with the coordinator. Sentinel must report pending/unverifiable evidence rather than converting a targeted test into a whole-release pass.

## Agent and model allocation

Prefer the host's inherited model unless a bounded job benefits from a deliberate smaller override. The currently exposed delegation runtime permits `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol` and the parent frontier model; do not rely on unavailable role-card model names or promise costs/latencies.

| Work | Allocation | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paths, symbols, test commands and branch/CI inventory | `gpt-6-luna`, low effort, recon | Read-only deterministic inventory; no architectural verdict |
| Shell installer fixtures, link/schema checks, fixed doc edits | Small model at low/medium effort where the interface is fixed | Explicit files and expected cases; escalate failed reasoning instead of lowering verification |
| Straightforward parser/lock/auth correction | Workhorse model, medium effort; raise effort for alias/auth subtleties | One subsystem, fixed owner contract and native regression |
| Canonical identity, historical authority, DAG/proofs and partial-upload semantics | Coordinator/strong model, high effort | Own cross-crate interfaces and failure semantics; no concurrent competing models |
| Implementation once interfaces are fixed | Workhorse implementer, medium/high effort | One isolated task/worktree with no shared write set |
| Independent challenge/review | Separate workhorse reviewer, high effort for model/retry changes | Read final diff plus tests; never rely on the author's self-certification |

Start with two implementing workers plus one read-only reviewer/recon, not an agent per finding. Increase concurrency only when there are disjoint, unblocked tasks and the coordinator can inspect every result. A packet contains objective, persisted paths/hashes, owned files, exclusions, criterion/test cases, dependencies and a completion condition. Workers preserve other changes and return changed paths, commands, actual outcomes, skips and unresolved concerns.

For parallel lanes, shared specs, architecture/README/operator docs, changeset creation and the repository Cargo.lock are coordinator-owned integration surfaces. Workers return proposed amendments for those files rather than editing them concurrently; the coordinator applies them on each PR branch before its final checks. Reserve shared Rust source and integration-test files explicitly before delegation; serialize packets whose write sets overlap. A forked agent conversation is not filesystem isolation: verify its actual worktree before allowing writes.

No concurrent Cargo builds/tests locally, even across tasks. Reserve one build slot; use sequential scoped runs and reuse the shared cache. Read-only analysis, shell-only tests, review and drafting can run while that slot is occupied. Worktree/build-directory changes need approval where they change environment or resource use; they are not a reason to bypass the repository's build rule.

## Verification at each boundary

1. Record baseline and test prerequisites; write a failing reachable regression before the correction where feasible. Check the exact parent delta and structurally identical siblings.

3. Review the changed diff and evidence independently. For model/proof/retry work, use a deliberate fault or mutation targeted to the changed invariant; ordinary docs/shell checks do not need a generic mutation campaign.

Run relevant excluded checks explicitly and require their CI results. Do not describe a second policy-script run as extra coverage already provided by `just ci`.
5. After restacking, repeat applicable checks on the new combined revision. Live `just provider-contract` / fixture refresh need network and are outside ordinary CI; recorded/skipped/live evidence must remain distinct.

| Maturin | Co-located dynamic/static boundary; native mapping; built wheel/sdist metadata and clean installation |
| Release recovery | Tag/push/draft/upload/publication failures; full owner barrier; original trusted bytes retained |
| Registry completion | Partial Python file upload, conflicting bytes, yanked files, index lag and changed read/upload routes through production providers |
| Generated workflow | Intent-selected builds/placement, fresh native auth, unsupported builder rejection and one NAPI effect owner |
| Installation/DX | Explicit action version fidelity; complete Cargo binary inventory; fresh documented first-release timing including credentials/commits |

## Stack mechanics without new infrastructure

Use ordinary Git branches/worktrees and the existing PR workflow. No stack tool was found in the inspected repository configuration; do not require a new tool to execute this plan.

Default: open cumulative child branches against `main`, label the dependency in the description, and include the parent-only review range.
